rv.q: He is, to be clear, bloody good in Krapp’s Last Tape.
Gary Oldman is vividly engaging in Beckett’s bleak monodrama
Still, my colleague Dominic Maxwell was slightly underwhelmed when he saw the piece in York, and I have to admit I came away from this evening in much the same mood.

It is an understated performance that requires patience from its audience — much of the time Oldman is chuckling or grunting at something his former self has said; in other moments, he sits in silence.

He isn’t either as moving or as desperate as some of his predecessors in the role, adopting a richer voice for the recording and a reedy growl as the older Krapp querulously interjects about the younger man’s foolishness.
A fantastic evening that cements Royal Court's 70th year as one of its strongest ever, and certainly a double feature worth waiting for.

cn.t: Oldman's return to the stage after decades draws crowds, but critics are divided: some hail it as a fantastic evening cementing the Royal Court's strong season, while others find the rigidly faithful Beckett production harder to celebrate.
